ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a Darlington pair circuit, with two NPN transistors cascaded. The first transistor is labeled β=90, and the second transistor is labeled β=25. There is a 48 V power supply on the left side, with the lower end grounded; the upper/left node provides 48 V base drive and is connected to the transistor collector side. The emitter of the first transistor drives the base of the second transistor, and the emitter of the second transistor is grounded through a 100 Ω resistor. Current I2 is marked on the base branch of the first transistor. Reasoning calculation: According to the problem statement, the voltage drop of each base-emitter junction is taken as 0.7 V, so the emitter of the second transistor, that is, the voltage at the upper end of the 100 Ω resistor, is 48 V - 0.7 V - 0.7 V = 46.6 V. The current through the 100 Ω resistor is 46.6 V / 100 Ω = 0.466 A, that is, 466 mA. Taking this current as the emitter current of the second transistor, the base current of the second transistor is 466 mA / (25 + 1) = 17.923 mA. This current is also the emitter current of the first transistor. The first transistor has β=90, therefore I2 is the base current of the first transistor: 17.923 mA / (90 + 1) = 0.19696 mA = 196.96 μA, approximately 197 μA.
